title: schematic write + readback
observations: Placed a real device from the system library (search '0402' -> item uuid 1e1c274d..., create returned primitiveId 744247fef1283782, designator 'U?'), then created wire A2PROBE_NET, net label A2PROBE_NET, net flag A2PROBE_VCC and saved (save -> true).
Readback after save: components 58 -> 60 (device + net flag), wires 34 -> 35, flag found by name, label found via sch_PrimitiveAttribute.getAll (value A2PROBE_NET), device found by proximity.
createNetLabel returned null while the attribute was actually persisted: the only reliable check is a readback through sch_PrimitiveAttribute.getAll.

Creating a component from an existing component/symbol identity (libraryUuid empty or 'project', symbol uuid) hung >90 s three times; only the library-search-item path is usable in 4.1.78 half-offline mode.
sch_PrimitiveComponent.getAllPinsByPrimitiveId on a freshly created async component blocked one 240 s invoke, so the wire is a standalone segment at fixed coordinates instead of a pin-attached wire.
Each write is an independent invoke (create/wire/label/flag/save/readback) because a single long program can hit REQUEST_TIMEOUT and discard its result, hiding the steps that already succeeded.
risks: device creation must go through a library search item; identity-based create hangs
pin lookup on a not-yet-committed component can hang; wait or avoid
createNetLabel create return value is unreliable (null on success)
ok:true only means the code ran; every write needs a fresh readback
no typed idempotency: repeated create makes duplicates
